# Summary of Information on Philip Rubin
Philip Rubin is a distinguished researcher and science administrator specializing in speech and language sciences. He earned his BA in psychology and linguistics from Brandeis University in 1971 and completed his PhD in experimental psychology at the University of Connecticut in 1975 under notable mentors. Rubin's interdisciplinary work integrates computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological approaches, with key contributions to articulatory synthesis, speech perception, sinewave synthesis, and signal processing. He developed influential computational models such as ASY and SWS at Haskins Laboratories. He also played leadership roles in federally funded research projects and scientific organizations, including directing a major NIH/NICHD project and serving as co-founder and president of AVISA.
Beyond research, Rubin held prominent science policy positions, notably as Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the NSF and as Assistant Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, where he led initiatives in neuroscience, biomedical innovation, and science policy modernization. He has been active in ethics, human subjects research oversight, and scientific advocacy. Rubin serves on numerous boards and committees, including Haskins Laboratories and the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS), where he is currently past president. His work has been recognized by election to multiple fellowships and awards from professional scientific societies.
Rubin's personal background includes being born in 1949 in Newark, New Jersey, involvement in early music bands, and pursuits in photography. He is married to Joette Katz and has two children. Rubin's scientific influence extends into popular culture through recognition in sound synthesis media and artistic tributes.
